LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 PUNCTUATION (CAPITAL LETTERS AND QUESTION MARKS)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and question marks)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and question marks), part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we use the punctuation marks?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and question marks) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn- Learning independently is enhanced as they practise how to use the target punctuation correctly in writing.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as learners work collaboratively in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem) – Learners acquire a high level of self-esteem as they punctuate their writing correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the knowledge of punctuations in learning of Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Textbooks in print and in braille

• Audio recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology
